summary: Find the minimum cost to reach the top, paying cost[i] when you step on stair i and climbing 1 or 2 steps at a time (start at index 0 or 1).
mainInsight: The cheapest way to stand on step i is cost[i] plus the cheaper of the two ways to arrive (from i - 1 or i - 2). Define the cost of finishing from step i as cost[i] + min(finish(i+1), finish(i+2)) with finish = 0 beyond the top.

approaches.name: Bottom-up with two variables
approaches.summary: Iterate from the end (or start) keeping the last two values.

personalSolution.notes: Correct. A bottom-up loop with two variables gives O(1) space.

promptVariants: Which DP recurrence solves Min Cost Climbing Stairs?
What is the choice at each stair?
options: finish(i) = cost[i] * 2, doubling the cost at each step
finish(i) = cost[i] + cost[i+1] with no further recursion
cards.explanation: From stair i you pay cost[i] and move to i+1 or i+2; choose the cheaper continuation.

promptVariants: Why is the answer min(step(0), step(1)) and not step(0)?
cards.answer: You may start on stair 0 or stair 1 for free (before paying its cost), so the answer is the cheaper of the two starting options. The top is any index >= n (beyond the last stair), which costs 0.
cards.explanation: That is why the base case is i >= n.

promptVariants: Complete the statement: Time complexity with memoisation: ___
cards.explanation: n distinct states, O(1) work each.

promptVariants: How can memory be reduced from O(n)?
What do you actually need from earlier states?
cards.answer: Each state depends only on the next two, so iterating backwards (or forwards with dp[i] = cost[i] + min(dp[i-1], dp[i-2])) with two variables gives O(1) space.

promptVariants: Why does `step(i)` return 0 for i >= n, and why is `lru_cache` safe here?
What would break without the cache?
cards.answer: Reaching or passing index n means you are at the top; no more cost is paid. step depends only on i (n and cost are fixed), so memoising by i is valid. Without the cache the recursion branches twice per call and takes exponential time because step(i+2) is recomputed inside step(i+1).

promptVariants: What is the answer for cost = [10, 15, 20]?
cards.explanation: Starting on stair 1 you pay 15 and can climb 2 to reach the top. (15: start at index 1, jump to the top)

incorrectOptionExplanations.10: Starting at index 0 then stepping to 2 costs 30.
